text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The famous English clown JOSEPH GRIMALDI was born in 1779. He created the white-face clown make-up.
English playwright CHRISTOPHER FRY was born in 1907.
German statesman WILLIE BRANDT was born in 1913. He was chancellor of West Germany from 1969 to 1974.
The famous legs during the second World War belonged to BETTY GRABLE, who was born in 1916.
Rolling Stone KEITH RICHARD was born in 1943.
American film director STEVEN SPIELBERG, whose hugely successful films include "Jaws", "ET", "Jurassic Park" and "Schindler's List", was born in 1947.
US saxophonist BOBBY KEYES, a very successful session musician, was born in 1953. He played with HARRY NILSON, JOHN LENNON, ERIC CLAPTON, JOE COCKER and many others.
United States drummer with White Lion GREG D'ANGELO was born in 1963.
** EVENTS **
1737 : Master violin maker ANTONIO STRADIVARI died. He
created the standards by which violins can still be judged.
1825 : Tsar NICHOLAS I succeeded to the Russian throne.
1924 : Pope PIUS XI denounced the USSR.
1946 : Britain's Labour government won the vote on state

ownership and railways and ports were targetted as the first to be nationalised. PM CLEMENT ATTLEE committed himself to a rigorous programme of reform which would see the nationalisation of health, the Bank of England, coal mines, civil aviation, cable and wireless services, transport and steel manufacturing.
1952 : The United States' SUGAR RAY ROBINSON resigned as
world middleweight boxing champion.
1967 : British traitor KIM PHILBY was hailed as a hero in

the USSR. The former British Intelligence office had been a Soviet spy since 1933. He was liaison officer in Washington in 1949 to 51, when it was confirmed he was a double agent and asked to resign. He reportedly warned two other Soviet spies GUY BURGESS and DONALD MACLEAN that they had been discovered. PHILBY became a Soviet citizen and a general in the KGB.
1975 : There was Christmas cheer in Melbourne after all.
Beer deliveries resumed after a two-week brewery strike.
1983 : Former US president GERALD FORD made an appearance
in the soap opera "Dynasty".
1987 : In South Korea, ROH TAE WOO was declared the
winner of the first presidential elections to be held in 16 years. Student riots during the campaign claimed electoral corruption.
1989 : The EEC signed a ten-year trade pact with the
Soviet Union.
1991 : The first international project to save

rainforests was launched in Brazil. The World Bank, the European Commission and the Group of Seven leading industrialised countries granted Brazil 250 million dollars for conservation work on the Amazon basin. All projects such as establishment of national parks would be controlled by the World Bank and not Brazil.
